description: Minimal FastAPI app: an APIRouter mounted on a FastAPI app, one decorated handler, and one Depends() provider. Grades the three fastapi.yaml relationship rules that anchored on Route:<handler-function> — a name FastAPI Route entities are never minted under (Refs #6444).

expected_entities.name: /things
expected_entities.note: Route minted from the decorator PATH (fastapi.yaml source_patterns, name_group 2). This is the only name a FastAPI Route is ever minted under from a decorator — never the handler function.

expected_entities.name: router
expected_entities.note: Route minted from the APIRouter variable.

expected_entities.name: app
expected_entities.note: Service minted from `app = FastAPI(`. The ONLY producer of a Service name in fastapi.yaml.

expected_entities.name: list_things
expected_entities.note: The handler function. Minted by the generic Python extractor, NOT by fastapi.yaml — so a Route:/Service:-prefixed stub can never name it.

expected_entities.name: get_db
expected_entities.note: The Depends() provider. Also a generic-extractor Operation.

expected_relationships.note: #6444. The decorator rule must anchor its Route end on the PATH the Route entity is named by, and its handler end on the generic-extractor Operation. Killing mutant: restore source_group to the handler function (Route:list_things) — fromCands for Route:/things still resolves, but no DECORATES edge originates from it, so this row goes not-found.

#6444. Was Route:<handler> -> Service:<dep>; BOTH endpoints were unmintable (Service: comes only from `app = FastAPI(`, and the Dependency rule names the entity after the OUTER function, not the Depends() argument).
#6444. Was Dependency:<dep> -> Route:<handler>; both endpoints unmintable for the same two reasons.

The include_router rule is ALREADY correct — both endpoints are real minted names. What this row pins is the edge itself: that a ROUTES_TO Service:app -> Route:router exists in the graph with those exact endpoints. It does NOT pin fastapi.yaml's include_router rule. Measured: strawberry_graphql.yaml carries a byte-identical include_router rule (same source_type/target_type/groups) that emits the same edge, so disabling fastapi.yaml's copy outright still grades 4/4 — this row cannot detect a fastapi.yaml-side regression on its own. The duplicate rule is tracked in #6514, deliberately not fixed here. Second limitation: this row does NOT pin the rule's source_type token. Mutating source_type Service->Route still passes, because `Route:app` misses byKind and the bare name `app` then resolves through the byName/kind-hint fallback back to Service:app. The three #6444 rows above DO pin their kinds, because their bare names (`list_things`, `get_db`) are ambiguous across the Dependency/SCOPE.Pattern entities that share them, so the fallback cannot rescue a wrong prefix.
